text.p: The French Communist Party (PCF) has been recovering from a sharp popularity drop since it picked a moderate leadership but voters are still not returning, according to an opinion poll released on Tuesday.

The survey by the independent polling institute CSA, to be published on Wednesday by the Communist daily L'Humanite, said 31 percent of voters had a good opinion of the party -- up from 19 percent three years ago.
Nine percent said they would vote for a Communist candidate and 17 percent said they would not rule it out.
PCF leader Robert Hue, who took over from veteran hardliner Georges Marchais three years ago, won 8.6 percent of the votes in last year's presidential election.
CSA said the recovery of the PCF's image was stronger among educated and middle-class people than in the working class.
The once-powerful PCF lost much of its clout under Marchais, a 76-year-old Stalinist hardliner who ran it for more than two decades from 1972.
Dogged by ill-health and shaken by the collapse of Soviet rule, Marchais handed over the party reins in 1993 to Hue, who has modernised and liberalised the movement.
Marchais announced earlier this month that he would not seek re-election to parliament at the next general election in 1998.
